questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent a rig from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent a rig from rolling over, keep cargo weight as low as possible when loading. Also drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer, you should:
questions.explanation: When coupling a trailer, the correct steps are important for safe operation. After you connect the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: The ____ trailer is most likely to roll over if a driver turns too quickly.
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous. The last trailer is most likely to roll over during a quick turn.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need extra space on the road because they:

options.text: Drive more slowly than other commercial vehicles.
Are heavier than other commercial vehicles.
Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is especially important when operating a combination vehicle.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance can present challenges when driving over:
questions.explanation: Railroad-highway crossings are difficult to cross with trailers that have low underneath clearance. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially challenging to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply in an older trailer leaks away:

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, there will be no working brakes and the wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. These tractors are difficult to operate and drivers must be careful.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in its "emergency" position:

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is set to "emergency," the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a combination vehicle turns too quickly. To prevent rollover, keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: How can you check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Get out of the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, get out immediately and walk away from the tracks. Then call emergency authorities for help.

questions.question: What is one benefit of keeping cargo centered on a rig?
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading increases the risk of a rollover. Keeping cargo centered on the rig helps prevent this dangerous situation.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
Stop air from entering the air brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers in the air supply lines. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect do?
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can tip over trailers. The last trailer in a combination is most likely to roll over from this effect. Drivers should understand how their vehicle responds to this and drive carefully.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, the seals should be pressed together at what angle?
questions.explanation: When connecting glad hands, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: What do you test by putting the trailer air supply control in the "emergency" position?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before each trip. After checking that the trailer rolls freely, test the emergency brakes by pulling out the trailer air supply control (or putting it in "emergency" position). Gently pull forward with the tractor to make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The rear trailer detaches from the combination.

questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer's braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. When air pressure in the emergency line drops, the tractor protection valve closes and the trailer emergency brakes activate.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows the wheels to lock up.
It stops the wheels from locking up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. When ABS detects that wheels are about to lock, it reduces braking pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, what should the driver do?

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel left and right.

questions.explanation: If your trailer starts to skid, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. The trailer will straighten out once traction returns.
